name: Gravitic Shear Pistol GSP-7 'Tidal'
description:
The GSP-7 generates a localized tidal gradient — a microscale differential in gravitational field strength across a 15–20 centimeter target zone — using a pair of counter-rotating superconducting mass rings embedded in the weapon's cylindrical body. The gradient is projected as a focused columnar field approximately 3 centimeters in diameter at the point of emission, expanding to roughly 18 centimeters at optimal range. Within this column, the difference in gravitational pull between the near and far edges of the field is sufficient to impose significant shear stress on materials and tissue, stretching and tearing structures along the field axis without any projectile or beam making contact.

The practical effect on unprotected biological targets at full output is severe internal trauma along the field axis — tearing of connective tissue, rupture of fluid-filled structures, and in sustained exposure, fracture of cortical bone. The weapon does not burn, does not leave entry wounds, and produces no visible beam. Forensic examiners encountering GSP-7 casualties without prior knowledge of the weapon frequently misattribute the damage to blunt force or crush injury from environmental sources. This forensic ambiguity is the GSP-7's most valued characteristic in certain professional circles.

TESSERA CORPONATION produced the GSP-7 under a research and development program nominally aimed at materials testing — specifically, evaluating shear resistance in structural composites under variable gravitational loading. The weapons application was, by most accounts within TESSERA, an open secret from the second prototype. Current production is limited, the supply chain is deliberately obscure, and TESSERA officially categorizes the GSP-7 as a 'field gradient analysis instrument' in all public documentation.
specifications:
field generation: Dual counter-rotating superconducting mass rings
field column diameter emission: ~3 cm
field column diameter optimal range: ~18 cm
optimal effective range: 8–14 m
maximum effective range: 22 m (degraded gradient coherence)
biological effect full output: Internal shear trauma, connective tissue rupture, cortical bone fracture (sustained)
power source: Cryogenic superconductor cell, 9 full-output shots before cell replacement
cell replacement time: Approximately 4 minutes (thermal stabilization required)
weight: 1.8 kg
length: 31 cm
forensic signature: Blunt/crush trauma, no entry wound, no thermal or chemical residue
tactical_use: The GSP-7 is not a weapon for open firefights — its 9-shot cell limit, 4-minute reload, and relatively modest stopping power at single-pulse output make it unsuitable for sustained engagements. Operators use it for targeted removal of specific individuals in contexts where deniability is the primary requirement. The weapon's lack of visible beam or audible report (beyond a low-frequency hum during field generation) allows shots to be taken in crowds or controlled environments without immediate identification of the shooter or weapon type. Experienced operators aim for the torso to maximize shear contact with organ tissue.
cultural_context: The GSP-7 is rare enough in GLMZ that most street-level operators have never seen one. Its existence is known primarily through rumor and forensic anomalies — deaths that don't quite make sense to medical examiners who aren't looking for the right thing. Among high-tier fixers and corporate wetwork contractors, the GSP-7 is spoken of with the specific reverence reserved for tools that solve problems cleanly. TESSERA's official position that it manufactures 'field gradient analysis instruments' has become a dark joke in certain circles. Possession of a GSP-7 is understood to mean you operate at a level where the rules are written by whoever survives.
known_users: Intelligence brokers with access to TESSERA supply chains
A small number of independent operators who acquired units through extraordinary means
Unknown — the weapon's deniability makes attribution difficult by design
story_hooks: A prominent figure in GLMZ dies of what appears to be a catastrophic internal injury with no external cause — the players are brought in to investigate and eventually identify GSP-7 as the mechanism, leading them toward TESSERA's deniable operations arm.

A GSP-7 with a full cryogenic cell turns up in a location it has no business being — a low-tier criminal's stash — and tracing how it got there unravels a chain of deaths and cover-ups reaching into TESSERA's board.
TESSERA hires the players to recover a GSP-7 from a journalist who is about to publish documentation proving the 'field gradient instrument' designation is fraudulent.

A player character is accused of a killing they didn't commit — the forensic evidence matches GSP-7 damage, and someone has gone to considerable effort to place them at the scene, suggesting a high-tier actor who wants them neutralized or controlled.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, neo-noir pistol with a distinctly organic yet mechanical silhouette. The cylindrical barrel assembly dominates the upper profile, appearing almost like a focused lens or sensor array rather than a conventional gun. The grip tapers smoothly from the cylindrical muzzle section, giving it an almost biological aesthetic — something between a medical instrument and a precision tool. No visible barrel rifling or muzzle brake; the emission aperture is recessed and barely distinguishable. The overall impression is of controlled precision rather than raw firepower.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 31 cm (barrel-to-grip), Muzzle section diameter: 4.2 cm at widest point, Grip length: 10 cm, Height including control surfaces: 7.5 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively hefty despite compact profile — 1.8 kg feels substantial in hand, weight distributed toward the barrel assembly due to the superconducting mass rings. Not unbalanced, but distinctly front-heavy; the cryogenic cell adds dead weight that requires a firm grip.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite frame with reinforced titanium alloy around the barrel assembly. The superconducting mass rings are shielded within a hermetic cylindrical housing of brushed surgical steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal composite body with mirror-polished titanium accents around the barrel collar. The cryogenic cell window (rear of weapon) reveals dull blue superconductor material beneath transparent synthetic sapphire — a deliberate aesthetic choice suggesting the weapon's exotic tech. Scratches and handling marks show through the matte finish readily, suggesting weapons-grade durability over cosmetic preservation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: deep charcoal gray composite. Accents: brushed titanium silver, cryogenic cell window glow of pale cerulean blue.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized composite with embedded micro-texturing for all-weather grip purchase. Slightly tacky to the touch, designed to prevent slipping even with wet or gloved hands. The underside of the trigger guard features a subtle knurled finish.
distinctive_features: Recessed emission aperture on muzzle — appears almost like a sensor lens rather than a weapon port
Dual-ring thermal radiator fins around mid-barrel (subtle ribbing to dissipate cryogenic cold bleed)
Sapphire cryogenic cell window at rear grip, revealing luminescent superconductor material inside
Low-frequency hum indicator LED (faint violet, barely visible) embedded in grip safety
Absence of conventional sights — targeting reliant on integrated optic or neural link, sights are flush/non-existent
Field coherence adjustment dial on left side of barrel — micro-threaded, barely half-centimeter diameter
No visible safety lever; activation appears to be capacitive or biometric
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Minimal markings. 'GSP-7' engraved in small sans-serif font on the left side of the barrel collar. TESSERA corporate sigil (a geometric tessellation pattern) stamped faintly on the grip where it meets the frame. Serial number laser-etched on the interior of the cryogenic cell window, deliberately obscured by the blue superconductor glow. No model year or batch designation visible.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-used GSP-7s show wear on grip texture (friction marks from repeated drawing and handling), minor impact marks on the titanium barrel collar from equipment contact, and occasional micro-scratches on the composite from environmental exposure. The sapphire window remains pristine in maintained weapons; some examples show condensation rings from thermal cycling. Weapons in professional circulation are meticulously maintained but show battle-scars rather than showroom condition.
